sentences.text: If you press a wooden block onto a spinning tire, you have a brake.
But the block grinds the rubber, and smoke pours off the tire.
So you bolt a steel disc to the hub and squeeze that instead.
But your hand is too weak, and the disc keeps spinning at 60.
So you add a pedal and a pipe, and brake fluid multiplies your push about four to five times.
Push the pedal, the pads squeeze the disc, and the wheel stops.
But now every hard stop heats the disc until it glows red.
So you cut vents through the disc, and air cools it from inside.
Repeated hard stops from high speed can heat a brake disc past 500 degrees Celsius.
Add a brake light on a post that glows when you press the pedal.
Congratulations, you have built a disc brake.
